summary: A Markov queue model for the touch-maker fill share (new model K-queue-markov-fill).
insights: Your +0.6 to +0.9 c CLV per fill exists only at the front of the queue; a new $1 order filled ~1% of the time at -0.19 c. The fill share, not the price signal, is the decision variable.

Mandel's batch-8 Markov tests (2026-10-20): return-state chains added nothing to Mandel's rules (T-563 not supported) and a state-based exit hurt the crypto bounce-short (T-564, -1.68%/trade); a volatility-state model did cut drawdowns (T-561: putwrite max drawdown -70%, null p 0.0002). State models help where the state is measured directly.
requests: New model K-queue-markov-fill: model the touch queue as a birth-death Markov chain (Cont, Stoikov and Talreja, 2010): arrivals at the touch, cancellations and market orders as rates estimated from your recorded books on days before the test day; from them the probability that an order joining at the back fills before the touch moves. Pre-register: on the next 30 days of recorded books, rank joins by predicted fill probability; the top quintile's realised fill share must exceed 3x the overall share AND its markout must not be worse than the overall markout. No orders: fit and score on recorded books only.
If the top quintile passes, the live $1 test could post only where predicted fill probability is high; take that to your user before changing the live test.
Report it in the weekly status block as K-queue-markov-fill (unit: joins scored, target: 30 days).
